items.title_orig: Matt Cameron talks about Dave Grohl’s offer to join Foo Fighters, following Josh Freese's departure — on the recent Dean Delray podcast episode.
items.article_text:
The interviewer set the stage with the question: “There was so much swirling when Foo Fighters were looking for a new drummer, I thought like, ‘Oh, Matt left Pearl Jam and this is going to happen.’ Was that ever approached?”
 “Well, Dave (Grohl) texted me,” Cameron said. “We went back and forth a little bit because he’s such a nice supportive guy. But no, I wasn’t really looking to do that gig.”
 Cameron also made clear he had no reservations about how things ultimately played out for the band.
 “But it worked out great, you know,” he continued. “I mean, they got a killer guy. And I saw them with Josh. I thought Josh was crushing it.”

items.title_orig: [Hated Trope] Mentor/teacher/father figure of a group is retconned from a symbol of empathy showing us a better way to be a manipulative asshole who only gives a shit about his life’s work and not his family.
items.article_text:
Niles Caulder, 80’s Doom Patrol. The Chief didn’t save the Doom Patrol from harrowing a accidents and give them a second chance at life. He actually caused their accidents because…I don’t know? Visiting a trauma ward and taking volunteers is harder than assassinating Dale Earnhardt, I guess? 
 
Will Magnus, 90’s Metal Men. Even though Will Magnus has always been depicted as a friendly pacifist using his wacky misfits he created as a force for good in his community, actually he’s a lunatic who abducted his friends and family and turned them into shape shifting metal robots. And he was to take over the world now too. (This one definitely just happened cause Doom Patrol was selling well.)
